messages:
alex: Kicking off HealthWave enterprise POC thread. They want a 30-day eval with sustained profile and frequent spikes. Need a capacity plan + pricing by EOD.
priya: Quick confirm: PHI-in-scope, will sign BAA, they require VPC peering + KMS. Also asked if we can offer token redaction for logs.
dan: Traffic shape? numbers?
alex: Baseline ~350 RPS, median call ~120 tokens. Spikes to ~2k RPS for 3-7 minutes every ~4 hours. Regional requirement: US-West with AZ failover. Targets: p50 <100ms, p99 <700ms.
tom: Given spike pattern, recommend reserved baseline + autoscale. Baseline reserve to cover steady-state + headroom for short bursts so autoscale doesn't always get invoked.
priya: Model choice: they prefer redwood/phoenix-30b-quant (q4_8). Will accept redwood/13b-distil-v2 as fallback for extreme load. Context ~1024 tokens occasionally.
dan: Throughput estimates (conservative): phoenix-30b-q4_8 -> H100 ~= 420 RPS, A100 ~= 320 RPS, T4 ~= 90 RPS. So 2k peak -> ~5 H100s (round to 6 for headroom) or ~7 A100s. 13b-distil -> ~800-1000 RPS per H100.
tom: Proposed offer for procurement: Option A) Flat reserve 6 H100s. Option B) Reserve 3 H100s + autoscale to 10 H100s with burst credits (prewarm windows). We should show monthly cost delta and expected usage/overage.
priya: They specifically asked about prewarm latency and autoscale cooldowns. For this burst cadence I'd set prewarm window 8m before expected spike and cooldown 240s. Also enable fast preheat API to spin up warm pools.
dan: Routing policy: primary -> phoenix-30b; if queue depth > 50 or avg tail latency > 450ms, route new requests to 13b-distil or serve with degraded token budget. Add quality gate: fallback allowed if top-1 adequacy >= 92% of primary on held-out prompts.
alex: Can we quantify cost? Rough numbers for proposal (ballpark): Option A flat reserve 6 H100s ~ $180k/mo. Option B reserve 3 H100s (~$90k/mo) + expected burst credits/overage ~$40-60k/mo depending on spike frequency -> total ~ $130-150k/mo. Show sensitivity to spike count.
priya: Also include mitigation: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, token-level caching and request dedupe to reduce peak load. That can lower burst GPU needs by ~15-25% for their traffic mix.
tom: We'll include a billable preheat credit model: X preheat minutes per month included with commit, additional preheat billed at Y/min. Procurement asked for an example calc for 50 preheat windows/month of 8m each.
dan: Load test harness (k6) sample — baseline + repeated spikes (use to validate autoscale + preheat):
```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = { stages: [ { duration: '15m', target: 350 }, { duration: '6m', target: 2000 }, { duration: '4m', target: 350 }, { duration: '6m', target: 2000 }, { duration: '10m', target: 350 } ], thresholds: { http_req_duration: ['p(95)<800'] } };
export default function() { http.post('https://api.redwood/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({ input: 'healthwave test' }), { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <POC_TOKEN>', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }); sleep(0.02); }
```
priya: Legal/security asks: BAA signed, SOC2 Type II docs, KMS/HSM details, audit log retention policy, data flow diagram, encryption-at-rest + in-transit, and redaction options for logs. They also want proof of VPC peering config.
tom: Blockers: signed BAA, network peering approval on their side, agreed fallback quality metric, and commit term. We should propose a soft-start plan if peering delays happen (start in hosted with strict data retention and encrypted logs).
dan: Ops config to recommend: reserved_pool: 3 H100, autoscale_max: 10 H100, prewarm_policy: predictive, prewarm_lead: 8m, cooldown: 240s, cache: prefix+KV enable, hedging: enable 2nd replica for p99 protection.
alex: Action items: dan -> formal capacity calc + sensitivity sheet; priya -> security pack + dataflow diagram; tom -> draft contract language for preheat credits & overage; alex -> coordinate procurement and schedule SRE prep window. Check-in tomorrow 09:30 PT.
infra-bot: Reservation request submitted (res-9002) pending approver review.
priya: I'll run a quick pilot test tonight with the k6 script and post results.
alex: Great. Let's have numbers & slide deck ready for customer call Friday.
